item.title: [Due today] Defender for Cloud Apps switches the SaaS accounts integration with Identity inventory on automatically from 15 October
item.description:
Accounts from connected SaaS applications start appearing in the Defender Identity inventory without anyone opting in, so the inventory count, identity-based hunting results and anything keyed to that inventory change on a date Microsoft chose. A tenant that still uses the two scoped Defender for Cloud Apps admin roles is excluded, which is the same pair of roles Microsoft closed to new assignments on 4 October.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-10-15 · Before 15 October check whether the tenant uses the User group admin or App/instance admin role in Defender for Cloud Apps; if it does not, expect SaaS accounts in the Identity inventory from that date and tell the analysts who work identity incidents that the inventory will grow.

item.title: [Due today] The legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API (/security/alerts) stops returning data after 15 October, and its replacement does not return every alert the old one did
item.description:
A SIEM connector, SOAR playbook or ticketing integration that still polls /security/alerts will keep succeeding and return nothing: an empty answer, not an error. And moving it to alerts_v2 is not enough on its own, because alerts from a Sentinel workspace that is not connected to the Defender portal never appear there.

Graph · deadline 2026-10-15 · Before 15 October search application sign-in and Graph activity logs for calls to /security/alerts, move each caller to /security/alerts_v2 with SecurityAlert.Read.All in place of SecurityEvents.Read.All, and for every caller that relied on Sentinel-only or standalone alerts name the other route those alerts will take.

item.description:
The retiring extension mounts Key Vault secrets through a CSI driver with a service principal credential held on the cluster; its replacement drops that stored credential and instead keeps a copy of every secret in the Kubernetes secret store. item.title: [New] Pre-authenticated (tempauth) file URLs retire on 1 April 2027: Graph file APIs stop returning URLs with an embedded token, and a tenant control lets you test per application first
item.description:
A tempauth URL is a bearer credential in a link: whoever holds the URL reads the file with no further authentication for as long as it lives, and it travels through logs, proxies and tickets. Its retirement removes that exposure, and it also breaks every backup tool, migration tool, scanner and line-of-business script that stores, inspects or redeems such URLs or follows the 302 redirect. Applications that call SharePoint URLs directly afterwards need an Entra ID access token for the SharePoint resource, which also means their file access appears in sign-in logs where it did not before.
